notes.text: Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Rutger McGroarty has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Evgeni Malkin is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Trevor van Riemsdyk returned in their last game after missing 15 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

story.head: The Predators give up shots, and the Penguins take them
paras: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime in Pittsburgh on Oct 24. The Pens (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Thursday, and the Predators (11-6-5) lost 7-3 to Minnesota on Tuesday. Going in, the Penguins are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Predators fourth in the Central (tied for 12th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.381) says: their chances are worth about .538, and their finishing has held them back. The Predators’ record (.614) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.530), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). On the other side, the Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). The Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators, and the Penguins’ struggling power play gets a tough test from the Predators’ penalty killers.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 21 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 21 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Predators, Filip Forsberg (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring. Steven Stamkos (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, with six goals in eight games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24.
Sergei Murashov (2-5-1 / .893 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh. Juuse Saros (7-4-4 / .918 SV% in 15 GS) has been a rock in net for Nashville and is expected to start.
At home, Andrew Brunette likes to send Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Dewar, Lizotte and Brazeau.
